tasks.short: Keep our labour market and workforce benchmark data current.

today.trigger: A workforce planning request arrives or a regular benchmark update is due.
steps: Find relevant CBS, UWV, sector and purchased reports.
Download tables and collect site or agency updates.
Compare dates, regions, occupations and definitions.
Clean the figures in Excel and record their sources.
Load comparable figures into the reporting dataset.
drudgery: Checking the same websites for updates
Copying tables and fixing changing column names
Retracing where a benchmark came from
today.time_sinks: 77.9 hours a year in the supplied allocation; repeated collection and definition checks are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Scheduled downloads and standard mappings remove most searching, copying and spreadsheet cleanup.
lenses.autonomous: Check an approved source list on a schedule and ingest updates that pass schema, date and definition checks.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a regional labour supply view for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, with seasonal trends and clear gaps in coverage.
lenses.joy: Remove table copying so I can investigate why recruitment conditions differ between sites.
lenses.options: Show regional, occupation and agency benchmarks side by side, with comparability warnings.
lenses.altitude: I own the source register, mapping rules and quality thresholds instead of collecting each release.
reach: Prepare labour supply inputs for recruiters.
Maintain external assumptions for FP&A workforce scenarios.

tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a regional or sector benchmark actually represents our shift patterns, CAOs and local hiring market.
tasks.pattern_why: Use deterministic downloads and validation for tables; use a model only to extract proposed fields from narrative reports, with source references and checks.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled source check finds a new release or an agency uploads an agreed file.
steps: Retrieve approved sources through permitted downloads or available interfaces.
Store the original file, publication date, licence and retrieval timestamp.
Map tables deterministically and extract narrative figures into a checked staging table.
Validate units, geography, reference periods and changes against the previous release.
Publish passing records to the benchmark dataset and queue exceptions.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve new sources, changed definitions and uncertain extractions; routine validated updates publish automatically.
systems: Approved source endpoints and agency exports
Proposed scheduled Python or Power Automate workflow
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint source register and ingestion log, including original files, validation results and publication versions.

evidence.claim: Power Query supports repeatable import and transformation of structured external data.
Combining controlled source collection with checked narrative extraction is plausible, but Noordhaven's source coverage is untested.

risks: Different definitions make apparently similar benchmarks misleading.
Website changes, licensing restrictions or unavailable agency exports interrupt collection.
A model may extract the wrong period, unit or population.
research_questions: Which sources account for most collection time, and do they permit automated retrieval and reuse?
Can the benchmarks distinguish the three regions and relevant warehouse or transport occupations?
On historical releases, how many updates pass validation without manual correction?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in our reports and how to use it.

today.trigger: A dashboard, report, metric definition or access arrangement changes.
steps: Compare the released report with its previous version.
Explain changed calculations, filters and data freshness.
Update guidance and capture relevant screenshots.
Identify affected HR users and managers.
Send the update and handle questions.
drudgery: Updating the same explanation in several places
Answering repeated questions about filters and refresh dates
today.time_sinks: 75.9 hours a year; drafting, distributing and repeating explanations are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Generate audience-specific release notes and help text from the approved change record.
lenses.autonomous: An approved release triggers updated guidance and a notification to the relevant user groups.
lenses.ambitious: Give every report a current definition page, worked examples and answers to common questions.
lenses.joy: Reduce repetitive announcements and spend more time helping managers interpret difficult results.
lenses.options: Produce a short manager update, detailed analyst notes and a shift-friendly quick guide from the same facts.
lenses.altitude: I design the reporting communication standard and monitor whether users understand changes.
reach: Support HR administrators with reporting guidance.
Provide learning materials for manager reporting training.

tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a change to absence, retention or staffing figures needs a conversation because users may interpret it as a change in policy.
tasks.pattern_why: A model turns an approved structured change record into plain-language guidance; deterministic rules control recipients, permissions and publication.

in_practice.trigger: A report owner marks a release record approved.
steps: Read the approved change record, metric definitions and affected audience.
Draft release notes and help-page changes with links to the released report.
Check figures, links, prohibited personal details and required freshness statements.
Publish routine guidance and notify approved user groups.
Route sensitive changes and unanswered questions to me.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve sensitive metric, policy or access changes before distribution; routine notes use an approved template and exception checks.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint release register with the source change, generated text, checks, approval where required and notification outcome.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports workflows involving SharePoint, Teams and Outlook.
Drafting release notes from approved change records is plausible, but factual accuracy and audience suitability require local testing.

risks: Guidance describes a planned change that was never released.
Notifications or screenshots expose restricted employee information.
Automatically generated wording changes the meaning of a metric or policy.
Too many messages cause managers to ignore important changes.
research_questions: Are report changes recorded consistently enough to generate accurate guidance?
Which changes can publish routinely, and which require owner or HR Director approval?
Do generated notes reduce repeat questions in a trial with site managers?

tasks.short: Write clear specifications for HR dashboards, metrics and data feeds.

today.trigger: HR or Finance requests a new report or changes an existing one.
steps: Clarify the decision, audience and reporting frequency.
Inspect source fields and existing calculations.
Define populations, dates, joins, filters and access rules.
Write examples and acceptance criteria.
Review the specification with the requester and source owners.
drudgery: Chasing ambiguous definitions after development starts
today.time_sinks: 72.7 hours a year; documenting mappings and resolving unclear metric definitions are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Draft specifications from request notes, approved schemas and the metric glossary, with missing decisions highlighted.
lenses.autonomous: A new request generates a draft, a field-availability check and a list of unresolved questions.
lenses.ambitious: Make every important workforce metric traceable from business purpose to source fields and acceptance tests.
lenses.joy: Remove document assembly so I can resolve what managers actually need to decide.
lenses.options: Compare alternative definitions, such as retention measured from start date versus completed onboarding, before building.
lenses.altitude: I govern the metric catalogue and specification process rather than writing every section from scratch.
reach: Draft reporting requirements for HR business partners.
Translate payroll and FP&A questions into shared data definitions.

tasks.human_edge: Negotiate a useful, fair definition of 'productive and still here after 90 days' with managers, HR and employee representatives where relevant.
tasks.pattern_why: An agent can inspect approved metadata, draft mappings and propose tests, but business meaning and access choices need explicit owner approval.

in_practice.trigger: A reporting request enters the SharePoint request register.
steps: Read the request, approved meeting notes, glossary and source schemas.
Draft the purpose, grain, cohort, date logic, refresh requirement and access rules.
Check proposed fields against available extracts and flag unresolved assumptions.
Generate synthetic examples and acceptance tests, including late and missing records.
Submit the versioned specification for business and technical approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The requester approves business meaning; I approve feasibility, mappings and controls before development starts.
systems: Proposed agent in an approved environment
data_needed: Field dictionaries and available extract schemas
CAO applicability and effective dates where relevant
Agreed evidence for onboarding completion and productivity
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned SharePoint specification register with assumptions, source mappings, decisions, approvals and linked acceptance tests.

evidence.claim: SharePoint supports document versioning for specifications and approval records.
Schema-grounded specification drafting and test generation are plausible, but cannot settle disputed business definitions.

risks: A polished specification conceals invented fields or unresolved assumptions.
Incorrect joins duplicate employees or lose agency workers.
Productivity definitions encourage unfair comparisons across jobs or shifts.
Employee monitoring or AI-supported employment decisions may require OR involvement, a DPIA and EU AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Is there an agreed definition and observable evidence for productivity at day 90?
Can the current extracts link recruitment, employment and learning records reliably and lawfully?
How much review time remains when generated specifications are tested against completed requests?

tasks.short: Turn hiring, onboarding and retention trends into practical recommendations.

today.trigger: The HR review cycle starts or a site shows a material workforce change.
steps: Gather hiring, onboarding, retention, absence and staffing measures.
Reconcile cohorts, denominators and data refresh dates.
Compare sites, job groups and periods.
Investigate plausible explanations with HR and managers.
Write recommendations, limitations and proposed follow-up measures.
today.time_sinks: 71.3 hours a year; preparing comparisons and assembling narrative are the main assumed sinks, while interpretation remains substantial.

lenses.faster: Calculate standard comparisons automatically and draft a briefing that links each claim to its supporting table.
lenses.autonomous: A validated data refresh triggers cohort analysis, anomaly checks and a draft briefing for review.
lenses.ambitious: Track the full vacancy-to-day-90 journey by site and role, then evaluate whether changes improve successful hires.
lenses.joy: Spend less time describing charts and more time testing explanations with the people running shifts.
lenses.options: Compare onboarding support, recruitment channel changes and shift arrangements using explicit cost and outcome assumptions.
lenses.altitude: I design the evidence and experiment system used to improve hiring outcomes.
reach: Prepare diagnostic briefs for HR business partners.
Develop workforce scenarios with FP&A.
Help L&D evaluate onboarding interventions.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguish plausible explanations from causal evidence and judge whether a proposed action is workable and fair at each site.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic analysis supplies checked tables; an agent drafts explanations and options, with human approval before recommendations influence action.

in_practice.trigger: The reporting dataset passes validation and the monthly review is due, or an agreed threshold is crossed.
steps: Build comparable hiring cohorts and mark those with a complete 90-day observation window.
Calculate trends, sample sizes and uncertainty using approved code.
Generate candidate explanations linked to source tables and known operational changes.
Draft action options with costs, assumptions, tradeoffs and proposed evaluation measures.
Review the findings with me before HR and managers choose an action.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve the analysis and wording; the HR Director and relevant managers own workforce actions and any required consultation.
data_needed: Vacancy, offer, start and exit dates
Site, role, shift and employment-type mappings
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint analysis register with dataset versions, code versions, supporting tables, reviewed claims and action decisions.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports repeatable measures and filtered comparisons for workforce reporting.
Drafting source-linked analytical commentary is plausible; reliable recommendations still depend on data quality and human judgement.

risks: Seasonality, job mix or agency use creates misleading site comparisons.
Recent hires are incorrectly counted as retained before reaching day 90.
Correlations are presented as causes.
Small groups reveal individuals or invite unfair employee-level conclusions.
Extending the workflow into individual employment recommendations could change its AVG and EU AI Act obligations.
research_questions: Can vacancies, hires, productivity and 90-day outcomes be linked with adequate completeness?
Are cohort sizes large enough for useful site and role comparisons?
Do blinded reviews find generated briefings accurate and useful enough to reduce preparation time?
Which proposed interventions can be evaluated with a credible comparison group?

tasks.short: Check that HR reports match source records and answer the agreed question.

today.trigger: A source feed, metric or dashboard changes, or a reporting discrepancy is reported.
steps: Read the specification and select relevant test cases.
Reconcile report totals with source extracts.
Check joins, date boundaries, filters and permissions.
Ask report users to confirm that outputs meet their needs.
Record defects, retest fixes and document acceptance.
drudgery: Manually checking the same boundary cases
today.time_sinks: 67.9 hours a year; repeat reconciliations and regression checks are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Turn recurring reconciliations and boundary checks into executable tests with automatic evidence capture.
lenses.autonomous: Run checks after each extract refresh and model change; hold affected outputs when critical checks fail.
lenses.ambitious: Test every important metric across sites, CAOs, worker types and reporting dates instead of sampling only headline totals.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive checking so I can investigate meaningful failures and discuss usefulness with users.
lenses.options: Generate candidate edge cases for rehires, transfers, missing certificates, late entries and hires near day 90.
lenses.altitude: I own the quality standard, coverage and release gates for HR reporting.
reach: Provide payroll reconciliation controls with the Payroll Specialist.
Help the Controller test workforce cost mappings.
Support HR administrators with source-data exception lists.

tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the test oracle is correct and whether the report supports the intended decision, even when every technical check passes.
tasks.pattern_why: Most checks have structured inputs and explicit expected results; AI can help write tests, while production checks run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: A nightly extract completes or a proposed reporting change enters validation.
steps: Run approved completeness, uniqueness, referential integrity and freshness checks.
Reconcile totals against source control totals from the same reporting cutoff.
Execute metric boundary tests and access tests using authorised test identities.
Store results and block affected releases or mark existing outputs stale when critical checks fail.
Route failures for investigation and request user acceptance for changed business behaviour.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve test definitions and resolve exceptions; report owners accept changed business behaviour before release.
systems: Proposed SQL or Python test runner
data_needed: Source control totals and extraction cutoffs
in_practice.logs_to: Test-results register linked from SharePoint, including dataset versions, expected and actual values, defects and acceptance records.

evidence.claim: pytest supports repeatable automated tests and machine-readable test results.
Power BI provides a Test as role capability for checking row-level security definitions.

risks: Tests reproduce the same incorrect logic as the report.
Source and report cutoffs differ, producing false failures.
Access tests miss export permissions or privileged workspace access.
A technically correct report fails to answer the user's business question.
research_questions: Are independent source control totals available at matching cutoffs?
Which past reporting defects would the proposed tests have caught?
Can the available environment test refresh failures and access controls reliably?
How much analyst time remains for exceptions and user acceptance after two reporting cycles?

tasks.short: Compare how nearby employers attract and retain warehouse and transport staff.

today.trigger: Recruitment weakens, offer acceptance drops or an employment proposition review is due.
steps: Select comparable employers around each site.
Collect public vacancies, advertised pay, shifts, benefits and training offers.
Normalise pay periods, hours, allowances and CAO context.
Compare public offers with our recruitment and retention outcomes.
Brief recruitment and reward colleagues on gaps and uncertainties.
systems: Public employer career pages and vacancy sources
drudgery: Copying benefits and pay ranges into spreadsheets
today.time_sinks: 61.4 hours a year; repeated public-source collection and pay normalisation are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Extract comparable vacancy facts and calculate pay components automatically, with links to the original adverts.
lenses.autonomous: Monitor approved public sources and queue meaningful changes for review.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a local employment proposition view across all three sites, including shifts, training and contract security.
lenses.joy: Remove vacancy copying so I can discuss which differences actually matter to applicants.
lenses.options: Compare pay, shift predictability, travel support, training and contract options under several recruitment scenarios.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the comparison method and evidence standard rather than producing occasional competitor spreadsheets.
reach: Prepare market evidence for Compensation and Benefits.
Support recruiters with evidence about the employment proposition.
Provide HR business partners with local workforce planning inputs.

tasks.human_edge: Judge whether advertised offers are truly comparable and whether a response fits our CAOs, operating needs and employment relationships.
tasks.pattern_why: An agent can collect public evidence and propose comparisons; a person must approve equivalence assumptions and strategic conclusions.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled review runs or an approved source changes materially.
steps: Retrieve permitted public vacancy content and preserve dates and source links.
Extract role, location, hours, pay components, shifts and stated benefits.
Apply approved pay-conversion rules and flag missing or incomparable components.
Compare against our approved employment terms and aggregate recruitment outcomes.
Submit a sourced comparison and action options for review.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve comparisons before use; Compensation and Benefits, recruiters and HR leadership own employment proposition changes.
data_needed: Current CAO tables and our actual employment terms
Aggregate offer acceptance and retention outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint market evidence register with dated source extracts, normalisation assumptions, reviewed comparisons and decisions.

evidence.claim: Extracting structured vacancy facts and normalising explicit pay components is technically plausible.
Public adverts provide incomplete evidence of actual pay, working conditions and competitors' retention outcomes.

risks: Adverts bundle allowances or holiday pay differently and create false pay gaps.
Expired or duplicated vacancies distort apparent demand.
Public material cannot establish a competitor's actual retention or recruitment success.
Collection breaches source terms or licensed-content restrictions.
Employer coordination or sharing non-public pay intentions would create competition-law concerns.
research_questions: Do enough comparable local vacancies disclose pay, hours and allowances separately?
Can a reviewer reproduce the proposed normalisations from the original adverts?
Which observed differences align with actual offer declines or employee feedback?
Do source permissions allow sustainable automated collection?

tasks.short: Prepare accurate workforce reports for HR, management and required reporting.

today.trigger: A scheduled HR report, OR information request or applicable external reporting deadline is due.
steps: Confirm the audience, reporting obligation, definitions and cutoff.
Extract employment, recruitment, learning and agency data as needed.
Reconcile headcount, FTE, movements and absence figures.
Calculate the required measures and explain material movements.
Check access, obtain sign-off and distribute the report.
drudgery: Copying figures into fixed reporting templates
today.time_sinks: 58.2 hours a year; repeat extraction, reconciliation and pack assembly are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Generate recurring packs from a reconciled dataset and approved templates, leaving exceptions and sign-off.
lenses.autonomous: A reporting calendar triggers preparation, validation and routing to the accountable owner.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent workforce measures across the three sites, with clear employee and agency-worker coverage.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive pack assembly so I can explain movements and improve data quality.
lenses.options: Produce audience-appropriate views for site managers, HR leadership, Finance and the OR from common definitions.
lenses.altitude: I own reporting controls, definitions and lineage instead of preparing each pack by hand.
reach: Prepare workforce inputs for the Controller.
Support HR leadership with OR reporting.
Help the Payroll Specialist reconcile employment populations.

tasks.human_edge: Determine the correct reporting population and disclosure level, and explain sensitive movements responsibly.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations and templates produce the pack; an agent can assemble checked commentary and route exceptions, with owner approval before issue.

in_practice.trigger: The reporting calendar reaches an agreed cutoff and the required extracts are available.
steps: Select the approved report definition, audience and applicable reporting requirement.
Snapshot source data and reconcile employee, FTE and agency-worker populations.
Calculate measures with versioned rules and check totals, freshness and disclosure thresholds.
Generate the pack and source-linked commentary, flagging unresolved exceptions.
Route for sign-off, then distribute through approved access controls.
in_practice.human_gate: I approve reconciliations; the accountable HR, payroll or statutory reporting owner approves each official pack before distribution or submission.
systems: Proposed workflow and approved language-model service
data_needed: Confirmed reporting obligations, owners and deadlines
Employment records, hours and effective-dated changes
Approved absence dates and administrative status, excluding diagnoses
Agency-worker population and hours where required
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reporting register containing source cutoffs, reconciliation evidence, report versions, approvals and distribution records.

evidence.claim: Power BI paginated reports support formatted report outputs and exports.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI Report Builder and paginated reports

evidence.claim: A controlled recurring reporting workflow is plausible, but Noordhaven's obligations, data access and licences must be confirmed.

risks: Effective dates, retroactive payroll changes or missing agency records produce inconsistent populations.
A template is mistaken for a confirmed legal reporting requirement.
Absence reporting exposes health-related information or identifiable small groups.
Reporting automation is wrongly treated as satisfying Wet verbetering poortwachter case-management duties.
Nightly refreshes are insufficient for a report requiring a more recent cutoff.
research_questions: Which reports are actually required, by whom, under which definitions and deadlines?
Can current AFAS extracts reproduce signed-off historical totals, including retroactive changes?
Are agency populations complete enough for each intended report?
Can a trial pack pass owner review without additional personal data or manual reconciliation?

tasks.short: Keep HR reporting templates, definitions and reusable analysis assets current.

today.trigger: An asset changes, a new reusable item is created or a periodic library review is due.
steps: Locate relevant templates, definitions, queries and guidance.
Check ownership, approval status and current versions.
Compare duplicates and identify stale material.
Update metadata, links and review dates.
Archive superseded assets and notify affected users.
drudgery: Searching for the latest approved version
Fixing broken links and missing metadata
today.time_sinks: 53.3 hours a year; finding, labelling and checking existing assets are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Automatically index assets, suggest metadata and detect duplicates, broken links and overdue reviews.
lenses.autonomous: A changed file or scheduled scan updates the catalogue and sends exceptions to the correct owner.
lenses.ambitious: Give every important metric, report and template a named owner, approved version, source lineage and review date.
lenses.joy: Remove library housekeeping so I can improve the assets people actually reuse.
lenses.options: Show approved variants by audience, site and CAO, with explicit applicability instead of near-duplicate files.
lenses.altitude: I design the knowledge lifecycle and ownership rules rather than maintain every entry manually.
reach: Maintain template catalogue metadata for HR administrators.
Support L&D with reusable reporting guides.
Help Finance catalogue shared workforce models.

tasks.human_edge: Decide whether two assets are genuinely interchangeable and recognise when an apparent wording update changes contractual or policy meaning.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic scans handle versions, links and review dates; a model proposes summaries and classifications within owner-controlled publishing rules.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised library changes or a scheduled catalogue scan runs.
steps: Inventory assets within existing permissions and read ownership and version metadata.
Check links, duplicates, review dates and references to superseded material.
Suggest searchable summaries, tags and related approved assets.
Apply permitted administrative metadata updates and route content changes to owners.
Mark superseded assets after approval and preserve required history and retention controls.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine checks and permitted metadata updates run automatically; owners approve content, applicability and archival decisions, especially for CAO, policy and contract assets.
data_needed: Links between metrics, reports and source definitions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint asset register with version history, scan findings, metadata changes, owner decisions and archival references.

evidence.claim: SharePoint provides document libraries, metadata, version history and content approval capabilities.
Power Automate can trigger workflows when SharePoint files are created or modified.

risks: An obsolete asset appears authoritative because its summary is current.
Search summaries reveal information beyond the reader's permissions.
Similar templates have different CAO or site applicability.
Automatic archival hides an asset still referenced by a live process or subject to retention requirements.
research_questions: What share of assets already has a reliable owner, approval status and review date?
Can indexing and search preserve existing document permissions throughout retrieval and summarisation?
Which metadata changes are safe to automate, and which require owner review?
Does a pilot reduce time spent finding approved assets without increasing incorrect reuse?

role.altitude: Owner of the workforce evidence system: shared definitions, reliable data flows, reporting controls and evaluation of changes to hiring and onboarding.
reach: Recruiter: labour market evidence, recruitment funnel diagnostics and channel evaluation.
HR Business Partner: site workforce briefs and evaluation of retention interventions.
Payroll Specialist and Controller: workforce population and cost reconciliation controls.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: sourced comparisons of advertised employment terms.
Learning and Development Specialist: onboarding completion and certificate reporting.
FP&A Analyst: workforce supply, hiring and staffing-cost scenarios.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 538.6 hours a year, about 33.7% of the implied 1,600-hour role. The proposed savings total approximately 370 hours, or 23.1% of the whole role, with capacity worth about EUR 28,865 at EUR 78/hour; this is not a cash saving. Current workflows and gains are planning assumptions for this fictional company. Speedups estimate each complete task after inputs become available, including automation and human review; they do not shorten the nightly source-refresh wait. Setup, maintenance, licences and approval delays could reduce gains. Accountability for employment decisions, medical judgement, payroll approval and OR consultation remains with the responsible people.
skills_to_grow: SQL, data modelling and effective-dated workforce data
Power BI measures, access controls and automated validation
AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube interface and export assessment
Python or workflow automation with monitoring and exception handling
Cohort analysis, uncertainty and practical experiment design
Source-grounded model evaluation and factual verification
AVG purpose limitation, minimisation and health-data restrictions
OR consultation and consent requirements, CAO interpretation boundaries and EU AI Act use-case assessment
Clear analytical communication and metric governance
role.ambitious_version: Build a governed vacancy-to-day-90 evidence loop across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Link recruitment, employment and onboarding records where lawful, agree observable productivity evidence with managers, and test which interventions increase successful hires. Use the recovered capacity to improve definitions, close data gaps and evaluate changes with HR, Finance and the OR; assess privacy and AI obligations before introducing employee monitoring or AI-supported employment decisions.
